title: Hartree--Fock coercivity for twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: We study the minimisers of the Hartree--Fock functional for flat bands in the chiral model of twisted bilayer graphene introduced by Tarnopolsky, Kruchkov, and Vishwanath. Our model is a continuous version of the discrete model considered by Becker, Lin and Stubbs in previous works and the first result is a direct analogue of main theorems of those papers: at half filling of the flat band of multiplicity two, there are exactly two minimisers, obtained by occupying either one of the two sub-bands. (A more general version of this result, stressing its topological origins, was presented in Appendix A.8 of the Lecture Notes by Tao-Zworski.) The new contribution is the strict coercivity of the Hessian of the Hartree--Fock functional at the two minimisers. It is a consequence of the difference between the Chern numbers of the component bands and can be optimistically considered as a soft version of a ``spectral gap''.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the stability of correlated electron states in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) using the Hartree-Fock approximation. It proves that the system's ground state is stable by demonstrating that the Hessian of the energy functional is strictly positive definite (coercive) at the expected minimizers. This mathematical result provides a deep theoretical underpinning for the insulating behavior observed in these correlated materials.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the stable ground states (minimizers) and proving the stability (coercivity) of the Hartree-Fock energy functional for flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene.
main_result: The minimizers are proven to correspond exactly to filling one of the two component flat bands, and the Hessian of the functional at these points is shown to be strictly coercive, indicating stability.
method: The analysis employs advanced mathematical techniques involving the study of projection fields on Hilbert manifolds, utilizing topological invariants like Chern numbers to establish a positive lower bound on the Hessian.
model_or_system: The system is Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) at magic angles, modeled using a continuous version of the Bistritzer–MacDonald Hamiltonian. The physics is governed by minimizing the Hartree-Fock energy functional derived by projecting electron-electron interactions onto the flat bands.
key_observables: The primary observables are the minimizers of the Hartree-Fock functional ($\Pi = \Pi'$ or $\Pi = \Pi''$) and the coercivity constant ($c>0$) of the Hessian matrix.
important_parameters: Magic angles ($\alpha$) where the energy gap closes, and the filling fraction (specifically half-filling of the flat band).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a simple magic angle and relies on mathematical techniques involving unitary trivializations and controlling variations in the projection fields.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows numerically computed lowest eigenfunctions for the first two magic angles. Figure 2 illustrates the curvature of the tangent line bundle at the minimizer $\Pi'$, showing enclosed curvature.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the flat band structure and the Hartree-Fock functional, then proving that the minimizers must be projections onto the component bands ($\Pi'/\Pi''$), and finally establishing the strict coercivity of the Hessian at these minimizers.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical proof of coercivity provides a strong stability criterion for the correlated electron state, which is crucial for understanding the insulating phases observed in magic-angle graphene.
